title: Method for conducting micro-abrasion wear testing of materials in oscillating sliding
author: Resendiz-Calderon, Cázares-Ramírez, et al.

steps.title: Polish material samples
steps.instruction: Polish each circular flat sample (20 mm diameter, 5 mm thick, ASTM F1537 CoCrMo alloy) until the surface roughness Ra is within 0.02–0.1 µm (target 0.03 ± 0.01 µm).

steps.title: Etch steel balls
steps.instruction: Etch AISI 52100 steel balls (25.4 mm diameter) in Nital solution (30 vol % nitric acid, 70 vol % ethyl alcohol) for 30 s to obtain a pitted surface with Ra = 0.4 ± 0.05 µm.

steps.title: Clean surfaces
steps.instruction: Rinse and meticulously clean both polished samples and etched balls with a suitable solvent (acetone or alcohol) to remove contaminants.

steps.title: Prepare abrasive slurry
steps.instruction: Disperse angular F‑1200 SiC particles (size 4–10 µm, typical 4–8 µm) in deionized water; stir magnetically until homogeneous. Use 80–120 g / 100 ml for rolling abrasion (high abrasive particle concentration, HAPC) or <4 g / 100 ml for grooving (low abrasive particle concentration, LAPC). Keep the slurry agitated continuously during testing.

substeps.instruction: Add the required mass of SiC particles to the measured volume of water.
Stir with a magnetic bar until the particles are uniformly dispersed.
Maintain continuous agitation while the slurry is in use.

steps.title: Configure tester
steps.instruction: Set the micro‑abrasion tester to generate an oscillating ball movement with a 12 mm arc length and 1.25 Hz frequency. Connect a peristaltic pump capable of delivering slurry at a constant feed rate of 0.5 g / min.

steps.title: Mount sample and ball
steps.instruction: Secure the polished sample in its holder on the tester and position the etched ball opposite the sample as illustrated (Fig. 2a,b).

steps.title: Perform preliminary tests
steps.instruction: Run oscillatory tests at sliding distances of 1, 3, 5, 10, 20 m for both HAPC and LAPC conditions, replicating each distance three times. Identify the minimum distance that yields a steady wear state (≥10 m in this study).

substeps.instruction: Record wear rate for each sliding distance.
Determine the distance at which the wear rate stabilises.

steps.title: Run micro‑abrasion test
steps.instruction: Execute the wear test under the selected condition (HAPC or LAPC, unidirectional or oscillating) using the steady‑state sliding distance identified earlier. Apply slurry continuously at 0.5 g / min, dripping it onto the ball near the sliding contact. Rotate the ball transversally every 20 m for unidirectional tests or every 2.75 m for oscillating tests.

substeps.instruction: Start the peristaltic pump to feed slurry.
Monitor the ball rotation interval and trigger transverse rotation at the specified distances.

steps.title: Repeat experiments
steps.instruction: Repeat the full test for each condition at least three times; verify that the standard deviation of the measured wear volume does not exceed 15 %.

steps.title: Post‑test cleaning
steps.instruction: Dismount the sample, rinse it with pressurized water to remove residual slurry, then clean again with acetone.

steps.title: Analyze wear scar
steps.instruction: Examine the wear scar on the sample by optical microscopy; measure the mean crater diameter (b) and calculate volume loss and specific wear rate using the provided equations.

steps.title: Report wear metrics
steps.instruction: Calculate and report specific wear rate, wear coefficient, and wear resistance for each tested condition.
